scope: Original 1.8 ARM64 script socket policy and HTTP defaults

provenance.source: Active IDA ARM64 decompiler and instruction view

policy_format.implementation_note: The range branches compare the comma-separated entry index, not the requested port.

global_values.name: data_TSocket_allowedbindzero
global_values.value_note: The static storage value is not treated as a runtime default without a startup capture.

functions.name: TSocket_checkAllowConnect_TString_const_int
functions.evidence: Delegates to IsHostAndPortInList with data_TSocket_allowedsocketsconnect before native connection allocation.

functions.name: IsHostAndPortInList_TString_const_TString_const_int
functions.evidence: Accepts wildcard, comma-separated entries, exact or pattern-matched hosts, exact decimal ports, and slash-separated ranges.

functions.name: TSocket_connect_TString_const_int
functions.evidence: Checks policy first, logs a blocked connection when denied, and otherwise allocates TSocketConnection and copies script TLS fields.

functions.name: TSocket_checkAllowBind_int
functions.evidence: Accepts wildcard, conditionally handles port zero, and scans allowedportsbind for exact or range entries.

functions.name: TSocket_bind_int_bool
functions.evidence: Checks bind policy before allocating TSocketConnection, calls bindSocket, and raises onBind or onBindFailed.

functions.name: TSocketConnection_bindSocket_int_bool
functions.evidence: Creates AF_INET TCP or UDP sockets, binds a zeroed sockaddr with the requested port, and calls listen with backlog 10 for TCP.

functions.name: TSocket_clearStaticStrings
functions.evidence: Clears the process-global bind and outbound policy TString objects.

functions.name: TSocket_setAllowedPortsBind
functions.evidence: Assigns the supplied TString to data_TSocket_allowedportsbind.

functions.name: TSocket_setAllowedSocketsConnect
functions.evidence: Assigns the supplied TString to data_TSocket_allowedsocketsconnect.

functions.name: THTTPRequest_runScript_void
functions.evidence: Uses the selected web-download limit after response parsing and participates in the ten-attempt redirect state machine.

instruction_evidence.meaning: Initializes the outbound allowlist entry index
Converts the requested outbound port for exact comparison
Compares the outbound entry index with the parsed range end
Compares the outbound entry index with the parsed range start
Initializes the bind allowlist entry index
Converts the requested bind port for exact comparison
Compares the bind entry index with the parsed range end

The native bind address is IPv4 wildcard address 0.0.0.0

observations.title: Configured socket port ranges compare the allowlist index instead of the requested port
evidence: The outbound range branch uses W21, initialized as the list index, at 0x207ad4 and 0x207ae0 instead of requested port W26.
The bind range branch uses W20, initialized as the list index, at 0x20591c and 0x205924 instead of requested bind port W26.
Exact decimal port entries use the requested port and are not covered by this specific defect.
observations.impact: A configured range can deny its intended port or allow an unintended port when the entry index falls inside the range. A repair should compare the requested port and reject malformed ranges before use.
observations.limits: No untrusted production script was run and no live network or listener was opened.

observations.title: An activated script can request a wildcard-address listener when policy permits
evidence: The script property table exposes bind, connect, send, and sendudp.
The bind path reaches TSocketConnection_bindSocket after its configurable policy gate.
The native sockaddr address is zeroed before the requested port is written, and TCP uses listen backlog 10.
observations.impact: A signed or otherwise activated script with a permissive policy may expose a local TCP or UDP service beyond loopback. A repair should disable listener creation for untrusted content and require an explicit approved-address policy.
observations.limits: Stock startup did not invoke bind in the reviewed local replay, and no external connection was observed.

observations.title: Selected web downloads are limited to 100 MiB and the HTTP pool defaults to ten requests
evidence: The selected-download guard occurs after response parsing and is not a general response-buffer, header, or unknown-length cap.
observations.impact: These defaults provide useful operating limits but do not replace independent HTTP framing and aggregate-memory limits.
observations.limits: No malformed response was fuzzed and no live endpoint was contacted.

interpretation: Exact host and port entries are a real pre-socket gate for script outbound connections.
Slash-separated port ranges are not reliable because both range branches use the allowlist entry index.
The script listener surface is conditional and remains behind package activation in the stock workflow.
The 100 MiB selected-download guard and ten-request pool default are useful operating limits, not substitutes for a general HTTP framing budget.
